title: Chemical Neurotransmission I: Synaptic Organization and Vesicle Release
method: Retrieved draft HTML and counted Unicode lexical tokens in p.teaching-prose only; visible article count separately excludes SVG and buttons, includes supplementary text. Final candidate changes robots metadata only.

comparator.comparison: Comparable substantial original paragraph-level exposition, with 17 theory sections and progressive experimental and quantitative reasoning.

scope_review: Synaptic compartments and direction; electrical versus chemical communication; action potential arrival and voltage-gated calcium entry; vesicle filling, docking and priming; SNAREs, synaptotagmin, fusion pore and quantal release; ACh and glutamate examples; perturbations and experimental interpretation. Detailed postsynaptic and termination mechanisms reserved for 4.B.08–09.
review_pass_1: Internal scientific and syllabus review: checked channel/sensor topology, docking versus priming, SNARE helix stoichiometry, trans/cis complexes, ATP and proton-gradient energetics, calcium-dependent fusion, spontaneous and asynchronous caveats, binomial assumptions and conditional interpretations. Historical records and accessible scientific literature checked.
review_pass_2: Re-read teaching and practice; added nine substantive paragraphs with electrochemical energy, variance-mean derivations and additional controls; revised distractors across Part B; added explicit causes of misconceptions and dark-theme SVG fill adaptation; repeated retrieved HTML audit.

arithmetic_checks.scope: Recomputed mean, failure, variance, Poisson, diffusion, Hill, power-law ratios, proton energy and inference parameters and question values.

academic_self_review.method: Two internal editorial passes, not external peer review. Deductions: incomplete full primary-source access (1), selected mechanistic details intentionally scoped to NET/SET and some conceptual reinforcement (1), simplified hypothetical models (1), no external examiner calibration (1), no interactive browser/accessibility test (1).

limitations: MP SET alignment uses archived 2024 copy, not independently confirmed newer primary MPPSC source.
Some NCBI textbook pages challenged full access; scientific records, excerpts and accessible reviews consulted; not every source read in full.
Static markup and source-level accessibility checks; no interactive browser/device or external expert review.
